title: Wall-clock performance assertions make the suite environment-dependent
reasoning: Several tests assert strict elapsed-time or memory ceilings using `time.time()` and `tracemalloc` while also constructing large datasets in-process. Thresholds such as 0.1s, 0.2s, 0.3s, 0.5s, and fixed memory caps can fail on slower CI workers, debug builds, shared runners, or Docker filesystem/database overhead without any product regression. This turns performance observations into flaky release gates.
reproduction: Run the performance-tagged tests on a loaded or slower Docker/CI host; the same endpoint behavior can cross the fixed elapsed-time thresholds and fail nondeterministically.
recommendation: Keep correctness assertions in normal CI and move strict benchmarks to a dedicated performance job with controlled hardware and historical baselines. For unit tests, prefer query-count assertions or broad smoke thresholds that only catch pathological regressions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: These tests are the source of the flakiness; they validate timing directly instead of isolating deterministic performance signals.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fast CI test that verifies query counts or bounded result sizes, and run wall-clock benchmark thresholds only in an opt-in performance workflow.
minimumFixScope: Adjust the performance assertions in the affected test modules or mark them so they are excluded from default CI.
